newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn suspends plan to quit U.N. development agency.
newsitem.headline: Bonn suspends plan to quit U.N. development agency.

text.p: Germany is set to suspend plans to quit a United Nations development agency which Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel feared would damage Bonn's chances of becoming a permanent member of the U.N. Security Council.

A foreign ministry spokesman said on Tuesday that Kinkel and Development Minister Carl-Dieter Spranger had agreed on a joint proposal to present to the cabinet on Wednesday which took Kinkel's concerns into account.

The daily Handelsblatt said this meant Germany would stay in UNIDO, the United Nations Industrial Development Organisation which promotes industrialisation in developing countries, for a year while it considered whether the body was reforming itself.
Spranger said last month that 1997 budget cuts had forced him to opt for withdrawal, the first time Bonn would have quit any U.N. agency.

But Kinkel argued that Bonn's 21 million mark annual contribution, about 22 percent of UNIDO's budget, was small compared to the possible damage that withdrawal would inflict on Germany's bid to join the Security Council.
Interest in UNIDO has waned worldwide as budget-conscious governments seek to cut costs.

The United States is pulling out at the end of this year, and Britain said on Monday it would quit at the end of 1997, although it planned to review the decision in a year's time in the light of progress on U.N. reform in general.

Spranger said last month that UNIDO, based in Vienna, had missed the world shift towards private enterprise that came after the fall of communism, and ignored calls to reform itself from a bureaucracy promoting state-run industry.
